rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) – source of lawful income protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent or mortgage payment, so they cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment solely because of that income source.
rules.penalty: Complaints may be filed free with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or in NJ Superior Court within two years of the alleged violation.

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_two_family
exempt_if.text: The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied by the owner as his/her residence at the time of such rentals

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_one_family_room_rental
exempt_if.text: The rental of a room or rooms to another person or persons by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as his/her residence at the time of such rental

coverage.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, including open land, for business or residential purposes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts rental of one unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, among other LAD exceptions.

rules.quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
